name: Sarcopenia
rawContent:
# Sarcopenia

## 1. OVERVIEW
Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength associated with ageing and disease, increasing frailty, falls and functional dependency.

## 2. RECOGNITION
Key features: reduced muscle strength (handgrip), slow gait speed, difficulty rising from a chair. Screening: SARC-F questionnaire, handgrip dynamometry, gait speed.

## 3. INVESTIGATION
Assess: handgrip strength, gait speed, timed up-and-go, calf circumference. Consider DXA or bioimpedance for muscle mass if available. Identify reversible contributors (malnutrition, vitamin D deficiency, inactivity, chronic disease).

## 4. MANAGEMENT
Non-pharmacological: progressive resistance exercise, physiotherapy, protein-enriched diet (1.0–1.2 g/kg/day or per specialist guidance), optimise vitamin D and treat underlying causes.
Pharmacological: no routine licensed drug; treat contributory conditions (optimize heart failure, treat hypothyroidism, address inflammation). Consider specialist trials or endocrine causes when appropriate.

## 5. PROGNOSIS
Associated with increased falls, hospitalization, loss of independence and mortality. Early detection and exercise-based interventions improve outcomes.

## 6. FOUNDATION DOCTOR ROLE
Screen at-risk patients, initiate basic investigations (nutrition, vitamin D, thyroid, inflammatory markers), refer to physiotherapy and geriatric/multidisciplinary services, and promote exercise and nutrition interventions.

overview.definition: Progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength and function associated with ageing and disease.
overview.epidemiology: Common in older adults; prevalence increases with age and comorbidity.
overview.pathophysiology: Age-related muscle fibre loss, reduced anabolic signalling, chronic inflammation and reduced physical activity.

keyFeatures: Slow gait speed (<0.8 m/s often abnormal)
Difficulty rising from a chair or reduced physical performance
screeningTools: Timed Up and Go / gait speed

initial: Blood tests: FBC, U&E, LFTs, TSH, vitamin D, CRP
Assess mobility: gait speed, chair-stand test, handgrip
specialist: DXA or bioimpedance for muscle mass if available
Consider referral for multidisciplinary sarcopenia clinic

nonPharmacological: Optimise protein intake and treat malnutrition
pharmacological: No routine disease-modifying drugs; treat underlying causes and optimise comorbidities
referral: Physiotherapy, dietetics, geriatric medicine as needed

content.prognosis: Improvement possible with early, sustained exercise and nutrition; untreated sarcopenia increases frailty and healthcare use.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Screen older patients, start basic tests, provide brief advice on exercise and nutrition, and refer to physiotherapy/dietetics or geriatrics for comprehensive management.
